headline: No break on the chart: foggy Saturday is the better bluefin day
body:
No advisories are posted, but fog is the real hazard: areas of dense fog with visibility a mile or less across the outer waters this morning, patchy dense fog in the channel after midnight, and patchy fog again Sunday morning. Run slow and keep the radar on. Today the channel is light with 2 ft seas, 2.8 ft in the triangle, 6 kn WNW by noon and gusts to 10 late. Sunday is a touch smoother at 2.6 ft, but the west breeze is up from dawn at 7 kn and 9 gusting 12 by afternoon, with Rachel's southerly swell filling in.

The honest call: the 64–68 band isn't anywhere on this chart. Triangle corners read 71.1 west, 71.8 at the south point and 72.1 east today, all warmer Sunday. Santa Rosa Flats is the coolest water anywhere at 70.7 and still three degrees over. If you go, go today, start the west corner south of Santa Cruz on that 71.1 and hunt bait. Don't burn 68 nm to Osborn — it's the warmest water out there at 72.6.
